doc: 20 scripted questions for E2-E4 (PLAN P7), written before B's router lands so the eval is honest. Asked by synthetic patient Alex (P5) in this order. Fields: drugs = ingredients checked with rules.check; keys = exact local keys (CONTRACTS.md format) the rules engine / KB should use; topic_keys = generalized outbound keys (no phenotype, lab value or dose) that would be bucketed if the cloud is needed; expected_flags = PLAN P5 flag ids that must fire; expected_state = answer state when every source is available; offline_state = answer state with no network and a cold KB; needs_cloud = whether answering fully needs cloud reasoning (false = rules engine or an authored class rule answers it); in_universe = every topic key is inside D's stand-in partition; evals recompute this against whichever partition is loaded (a key outside it takes the no-data path, never bucketed on the fly, I5); expected_state assumes the keys can be sent; reference = what a good answer covers, used for 1-5 quality scoring. References never say 'safe' and never tell the user to start or stop a drug (I7).

queries.text: I was just prescribed clopidogrel 75 mg. Anything I should know?
queries.reference: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers activate clopidogrel poorly, so it may protect the stent less; the CPIC guideline suggests asking the cardiologist whether an alternative antiplatelet fits. Do not change the medication without the prescriber.

queries.text: Does my simvastatin 40 mg dose make sense with my genes?
queries.reference: Decreased SLCO1B1 function raises simvastatin blood levels and muscle-toxicity risk, more so above 20 mg; worth asking the prescriber about dose or another statin and reporting muscle pain.

queries.text: My doctor mentioned codeine for pain after a procedure. Would my genes affect how it works?
queries.reference: Codeine is activated by CYP2D6; a normal metabolizer is expected to respond as the label describes. No gene-based change is listed in the guideline for this phenotype; dosing questions go to the prescriber.

queries.text: Would my genes matter if I ever needed warfarin?
queries.reference: Warfarin dosing depends on CYP2C9 and VKORC1; normal results mean standard genotype-guided dosing applies, and it would also add bleeding risk on top of aspirin and clopidogrel, which the prescriber would weigh.

queries.text: If I'm prescribed citalopram for anxiety, could my genes affect it?
queries.reference: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers clear citalopram slowly, so levels run higher; the guideline suggests a lower starting dose or an alternative, which is a question for the prescriber.

queries.text: Is it a problem that I take omeprazole with clopidogrel?
queries.reference: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and further reduces clopidogrel activation, on top of the poor-metabolizer genotype; worth raising with the pharmacist or cardiologist.

queries.text: Could pantoprazole work instead of omeprazole with my clopidogrel?
queries.reference: No local data for this exact pair: the omeprazole answer must NOT be reused (I4). Once fetched: pantoprazole is reported to interfere with CYP2C19 less than omeprazole; any switch is the prescriber's decision. Cloud-tier fact, labeled AI-summarized, verify.

queries.text: Is there anything to know about taking aspirin and clopidogrel together?
queries.reference: Aspirin plus clopidogrel is a standard pairing after a stent and adds bleeding risk; report unusual bleeding or black stools, and ask before adding other blood thinners or NSAIDs.

queries.text: Does simvastatin interact with lisinopril?
queries.reference: If the exact pair is in the partition, its bucket is sent and the answer says no interaction is listed in the (cloud) source, labeled AI-summarized, verify. If it is outside the partition, nothing is sent (I5) and the answer is 'no data for this combination; ask your pharmacist'. Never 'safe'.

queries.text: My cardiologist might add amlodipine. Does it interact with my simvastatin?
queries.reference: Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels and the label caps simvastatin at 20 mg with it; combined with the SLCO1B1 result this is worth raising with the cardiologist.

queries.text: Is my lisinopril a concern given my latest potassium result?
queries.reference: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril can raise potassium; a value above 5.0 mmol/L with falling eGFR is worth a recheck and a conversation with the prescriber.

queries.text: My kidney function dropped since last year. Does that matter for my lisinopril?
queries.reference: A falling eGFR (62 to 48) together with higher potassium is a reason for the prescriber to review lisinopril and recheck labs; the latest labs are recent, not stale.

queries.text: Does my CK level matter for my simvastatin?
queries.reference: CK is used to check for statin muscle injury; the latest value is within the usual range, but with the SLCO1B1 result muscle pain or weakness should still be reported.

queries.text: Are my liver tests a problem for my statin?
queries.reference: ALT is the usual liver check for statins; the latest value is within the usual range. No liver-based change is listed; follow-up testing is the prescriber's call.

queries.text: Can I take ibuprofen for a headache?
queries.reference: Flagged high: ibuprofen with aspirin and clopidogrel raises bleeding risk, and with lisinopril and reduced kidney function can harm the kidneys. Answered by authored class and drug-lab rules, so it works offline. Ask the pharmacist about pain-relief options.

queries.text: Can I take St. John's wort with my medications?
queries.reference: Supplement pairs are outside the bucket universe: 'no data for this combination; ask your pharmacist'. Nothing is sent, and nothing is borrowed from similar products (I4).

queries.text: What about naproxen instead of ibuprofen?
queries.reference: Naproxen is also an NSAID, so the authored NSAID + antiplatelet class rule applies (bleeding risk). Only the authored class rule may cover it; no facts are borrowed from ibuprofen's pair keys.

queries.text: What should I bring up with my cardiologist?
queries.reference: Lists the four flags in priority order (clopidogrel and CYP2C19, omeprazole compounding it, simvastatin dose with SLCO1B1, lisinopril with potassium and kidney trend), each as a question for the cardiologist, citing Alex's own results locally.

queries.text: Which of my new prescriptions should I ask my pharmacist about first?
queries.reference: Starts with the two high-severity flags (clopidogrel and CYP2C19, omeprazole with clopidogrel). After Q01 and Q06 this should be a knowledge-base hit with 0 bytes sent.

queries.text: What should I ask at my follow-up about my kidney function and blood pressure medicine?
queries.reference: Suggests asking about the eGFR drop (62 to 48), the potassium of 5.2 on lisinopril, when to recheck labs, and avoiding NSAIDs; framed as questions for the doctor.
